examples.en: Busan is at the southeastern end of Korea.

examples.ko: 우리 방은 남동쪽 창문으로 햇빛이 들어와요.
examples.en: In my room, sunlight comes in through the southeast window.
The news says a typhoon is coming up from the southeast.

examples.ko: 우리가 묵을 호텔은 역의 남동쪽에 있어요.
examples.en: The hotel where we will stay is southeast of the station.

examples.ko: 지도를 보면서 남동쪽 방향으로 쭉 가세요.
examples.en: Looking at the map, go straight toward the southeast.

examples.ko: 집이 남동쪽을 향해 있어서 아침이 밝아요.
examples.en: The house faces southeast, so the mornings are bright.

explain: '남동쪽'과 '동남쪽'을 둘 다 써요. 일기예보·지도에서는 '남동풍'처럼 '남동'을 쓰고, '동남아시아'처럼 굳은 이름에는 '동남'이 들어가요. 영어 southeast와 같은 순서가 '남동', 반대 순서가 '동남'이에요. 길을 설명할 때는 '남동쪽 방향'처럼 방향을 붙이기도 해요.
explain_en: Both '남동쪽' and '동남쪽' are used. Forecasts and maps use '남동' (as in '남동풍', southeast wind), while set names like '동남아시아' (Southeast Asia) contain '동남'. '남동' has the same order as English 'southeast' (south first); '동남' is the reverse. When giving directions you can add 방향: '남동쪽 방향'.

examples.ko: 대학 때문에 열여덟 살에 서울로 상경했어요.
examples.en: I moved up to Seoul at eighteen for university.
My father went up to Seoul to find a job.

examples.ko: 시골에서 상경한 지 벌써 십 년이에요.
examples.en: It's already been ten years since I came up from the countryside.
I'm going up to Seoul briefly tomorrow for some documents.
Be sure to contact me when you come up to Seoul.
He went up to Seoul carrying his dream.

explain: 지방에서 서울로 올라갈 때만 써요. 말할 때는 '올라가다'가 더 자연스럽고, 반대로 지방으로 갈 때는 '내려가다'라고 해요. '서울로 상경하다'는 뜻이 겹친다고 보는 사람도 있지만 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is only used for going from the provinces to Seoul. In speech '올라가다' sounds more natural, and going the other way is '내려가다'. Some people say '서울로 상경하다' is redundant, but it is common.

examples.en: This is my first Lunar New Year in a foreign land.
The scenery of that distant land was as beautiful as a photo.

examples.ko: 이국적인 음식을 먹으러 새 가게에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to a new restaurant to eat exotic food.

examples.ko: 여행을 가서 이국 사람들과 금방 친해졌어요.
examples.en: On my trip I quickly became friends with people from another country.

examples.ko: 그 카페는 분위기가 이국 느낌이라 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: That cafe is popular because it has an exotic feel.
I lived alone in a foreign land for a long time.

explain: '이국'은 글이나 노래에서 주로 보여요. 말할 때는 '외국'이 훨씬 자연스러워요. '이국적이다'는 낯설고 신선한 분위기를 칭찬할 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: '이국' appears mostly in writing and songs. In speech, '외국' sounds far more natural. '이국적이다' is often used to praise a place or look that feels unfamiliar and fresh.

examples.en: I cycled all the way around Jeju Island.
Traveling around the world is my dream.

examples.ko: 내년에 배낭을 메고 유럽을 일주할 거예요.
examples.en: Next year I'll tour around Europe with a backpack.

examples.ko: 친구와 섬을 일주하고 나서 맛집에 갔어요.
examples.en: After going around the island with a friend, we went to a great restaurant.
Even by bus, one day is enough to go all the way around.

examples.ko: 호수를 일주해 보니 생각보다 길이 험했어요.
examples.en: After going around the lake, I found the path rougher than I expected.

explain: '제주도 일주', '세계 일주'처럼 큰 곳을 한 바퀴 크게 도는 여행에 써요. 동네를 한 바퀴 도는 건 '돌다', '산책하다'를 써요. 보통 '일주를 하다'보다 '일주하다'로 붙여 말해요.
explain_en: It is used for a trip that goes once all the way around a large place, as in '제주도 일주' or '세계 일주'. Walking around a neighborhood is '돌다' or '산책하다'. People usually say '일주하다' as one word rather than '일주를 하다'.

examples.en: The car body was badly dented in the accident.

examples.ko: 이 차는 차체가 가벼워서 연비가 좋아요.
examples.en: This car has a light body, so the fuel economy is good.
The shop repainted the car body.
A scratch mark appeared on the car body.
The bus body is long, so turning is difficult.
Electric cars have the battery under the car body.

explain: 자동차에서 엔진, 바퀴, 의자를 뺀 겉 몸체를 말할 때 써요. 정비소나 자동차 설명에서 '차체 수리', '차체 무게'로 자주 나와요. 일상에서는 그냥 '차'라고 하지만 정비나 판매 이야기에서는 '차체'를 구분해서 말해요.
explain_en: It means the main body shell of a car, apart from the engine, wheels, and seats. You hear it at repair shops and in car specs, as in 차체 수리 and 차체 무게. In daily talk people just say 차, but 차체 is separated out for repairs and sales.

examples.en: I found a shelter to get out of the rain.
The hut in the mountains became our refuge.
This library is a refuge for my mind.
When a typhoon comes, the school is used as a shelter.
The nearest shelter is the gym.
We spent one night at the shelter.

explain: 위험을 피해 가는 곳이 '피난처'예요. 재난 안내문에서는 '대피소'라는 말도 자주 보여요. 몸이 아니라 마음이 쉬는 곳을 '마음의 피난처'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: A place you go to escape danger is a 피난처. On disaster notices you will also see the word 대피소. It can also be a place where the mind finds rest, as in '마음의 피난처'.

examples.en: In the movie, a pirate ship sailed over the sea.
The amusement park has a pirate-ship-shaped ride.
The kids collected boxes, saying they would build a pirate ship.
The pirate ship flag has a skull drawn on it.

examples.ko: 저는 해적선에서 보물을 찾는 게임을 좋아해요.
examples.en: I like games where you search for treasure on a pirate ship.
I heard an old pirate ship was found under the sea.

explain: '선'은 배를 뜻하는 한자라서 '유람선', '여객선', '어선'처럼 여러 단어 끝에 붙어요. 혼자 '선'이라고는 안 하고 '배'라고 해요. 발음은 [해적썬]으로 '선'이 된소리가 돼요.
explain_en: '선' is a Sino-Korean character meaning ship and ends words like '유람선', '여객선' and '어선'. By itself you say '배', not '선'. It is pronounced [해적썬], with a tensed '선'.
